item.title: MJR Morning Brief — November 13, 2026
item.description:
From Media Jobs Report, here's your latest media industry update.
Nielsen's 2026 Annual Marketing Report reveals growing concerns about advertising budgets. Fourteen percent of U.S. marketers now anticipate cuts, up from just 2 percent last year. With audiences spread across more platforms, advertisers are demanding better measurement and stronger results. The report also highlights continued digital advertising growth and the importance of reaching consumers across multiple channels. Read the full findings at Media Jobs Report dot com.
In television news,
TEGNA has promoted three veteran sales leaders to President and General Manager positions. Ryan Drake will oversee stations in Des Moines and Davenport, Iowa. Tony Motta will lead stations in Phoenix and Tucson, Arizona, while Angela New takes the helm at WVEC in Norfolk, Virginia. All three will focus on revenue growth, audience development and streaming.
Turning to radio,
Edison Research's latest Share of Ear findings show AM/FM radio and SiriusXM perform strongest in cars, while YouTube and audiobooks excel at home. Streaming music and podcasts perform especially well on the go. The findings offer advertisers new insights into where Americans listen throughout their day.
In radio news,
Audacy has named veteran sports radio host Zach Gelb Brand Manager of Miami’s 104.3 WQAM. Gelb will oversee programming, talent and station operations, including flagship coverage of the Miami HEAT, Marlins, Florida Panthers and Miami Hurricanes. The appointment follows WQAM’s first anniversary on FM.
Turning to streaming,
A new Gracenote study finds 78% of young adults want one program guide covering all their streaming services, up from 58% last year. More than half of viewers say they might cancel a service if they can't find something worth watching. The findings highlight growing frustration with streaming choices and subscriptions.
In radio news,
The FCC has reviewed 60 applications for its upcoming auction of 132 FM radio construction permits. Thirty-eight applications were complete, 21 need corrections, and one was rejected. Applicants have until December third to submit corrections and required payments. Bidding begins February second, 2027.
Turning to industry appointments,
USA TODAY has named Ryan J. Rusak its new Opinion Editor, effective November 30. Rusak joins from the Fort Worth Star-Telegram, where he's led opinion coverage since 2019. He previously spent nearly two decades at The Dallas Morning News. Rusak will oversee opinion strategy, expand contributor voices and grow digital and video engagement.
In podcasting news,
Charlie Sheen is stepping behind the microphone with a new weekly podcast called “Mostly Sheenius.” The series launches with Michael Douglas as its first guest, discussing Hollywood and their work together on “Wall Street.” Upcoming guests include Rob Lowe, Martin Sheen, Emilio Estevez and Denise Richards.
Turning to industry appointments,
ACA Connects has elected Melanie Hannasch of Vyve Broadband to its Board of Directors. Hannasch serves as Interim Co-President and Chief Operating Officer, overseeing operations across 16 states. With more than 20 years of telecommunications experience, she brings extensive expertise in expanding broadband access to rural and underserved communities.
And finally,
Jacobs Media is inviting radio stations across the U.S. and Canada to participate in Techsurvey 2027. The annual study will explore changing listening habits, streaming, artificial intelligence, and radio’s place in connected cars. Stations have until December 18th to register, with the survey launching in January. More details are available on Media Jobs Report dot com.
For more media news, the latest jobs, free media tools and more, log in to MediaJobsReport.com.
